summary: Append-only / version immutability is now enforced at the storage layer by one new forward-only migration (infra/migrations/00014_append_only_enforcement.sql) that creates a single shared PL/pgSQL guard function and a BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE row trigger per covered table. The guard RAISEs P0001 naming the table and the forbidden operation (TG_TABLE_NAME/TG_OP). Covered set (13 tables, append-only BY DESIGN per docs/21 §4, docs/46, ADR-007/008/021, Master Acceptance Gate A): scientific_object_versions, relation_versions, project_states, state_commits, releases, research_asset_versions, asset_lineage, policy_versions, validation_results, contribution_events, audit_log, research_events, external_reference_snapshots. The Supervisor's original tamper (UPDATE scientific_object_versions SET title/... ) is now rejected by the database itself with SQLSTATE P0001, proven against a real PostgreSQL via psql and by Go regression tests; DELETE is rejected identically; a legitimate INSERT of a new version row succeeds. Deliberately exempt (mutable by design, each justified in notes_for_supervisor): all current-state/workflow tables (users, organizations, memberships, programs, projects, scientific_objects, relations, branches, research_assets, issues, pull_requests, reviews, evidence_assertions, credit_disputes, subscriptions, blobs, blob_attachments, external_references, knowledge_publications, asset_dependencies), the worker bookkeeping tables (outbox_events, webhook_deliveries) and the rebuildable search projection (search_documents). No existing constraint was changed or dropped; no column semantics added; sqlc drift check clean; doctor.sh and make check pass; diff is exactly within allowed_scope.

acceptance.criterion: an UPDATE of an existing scientific_object_versions row is rejected by the database

Regression test TestAppendOnlyEnforcement asserts pgconn.PgError Code == "P0001" and the message naming the table and UPDATE.

risks: TRUNCATE is not blocked: row-level triggers do not fire on TRUNCATE. Most guarded tables are FK-referenced (scientific_object_versions, relation_versions, project_states, state_commits, releases, research_asset_versions, asset_lineage, policy_versions) so plain TRUNCATE fails with 0A000 there, but audit_log, contribution_events, research_events, validation_results and external_reference_snapshots have no referencing tables and a table owner could TRUNCATE them. Documented as a follow-up, not implemented (the owner-decided mechanism for this task is BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE triggers).

The guard is a database mechanism, not a security boundary against superusers: a table owner can still DISABLE TRIGGER / ALTER the function. This matches the intended model (defense against application-level and accidental rewrites, with an admin break-glass runbook per docs/9), but it is not tamper-proof against the DBA role.

The covered set is an L1 decision derived from the specs. If the Supervisor wants a different boundary (e.g. also guarding knowledge_publications, or exempting validation_results), it is a one-line change plus a new forward-only migration — no shipped file would be edited.

Over-guarding a table that a future product flow legitimately updates would surface as a P0001 at runtime; each such case would need a new migration. The current persistence query layer performs no UPDATE/DELETE on any covered table (verified: only outbox_events, blobs, projects, search_documents are mutated by existing queries).
follow_up_issues: Consider statement-level BEFORE TRUNCATE triggers (or explicit TRUNCATE tests) for the append-only tables that no FK pins: audit_log, contribution_events, research_events, validation_results, external_reference_snapshots.

Confirm the exemption boundary: knowledge_publications (publication/visibility record per ADR-006) and validation_results (gate-run record) sit on the edge of the append-only set; extending the guard to them later is a trivial forward-only migration.
notes_for_supervisor: COVERED (13 tables) — scientific_object_versions & relation_versions: version logs, docs/21 §4 '不 update semantic content；修正通过新记录', Master Acceptance Gate A; project_states & state_commits: the RSG state history (task requirement 'state commits'), docs/53 'UPDATE 不能覆写历史 scientific content' — current state moves via pointers (branches.base_state_id, docs/21 §5), never by mutating a state row; releases & research_asset_versions & asset_lineage: ADR-008 'Release 与 Published Asset Version 不可变', docs/11 §1/§2/§5/§7; policy_versions: 'Policy 版本化；Release 绑定当时 policy version' (docs/12), Master Acceptance 'policy/schema/version/hash pinned'; validation_results: each row is a recorded gate run (re-runs append — no unique constraint); contribution_events & audit_log: the append-only ledgers (docs/21 §4, docs/46, docs/13, invariant 14); research_events: ADR-021 'Append-only Domain Event Log'; external_reference_snapshots: docs/19 §2 'pinned snapshot' (re-access appends a new snapshot). EXEMPT — mutable by design: users/organizations/organization_memberships/programs/projects/project_memberships/scientific_objects/relations/research_assets (current state); branches (lifecycle_state active→merged→aborted and base_state_id current pointer); issues/pull_requests (state machines); reviews (workflow decisions); evidence_assertions (review_state unreviewed→reviewed→rejected workflow); credit_disputes (open→resolved→rejected state machine — corrections leave traces via the dispute record + immutable contribution_events); blobs (integrity_state pending→verified→failed); blob_attachments (access_level is a current access declaration); external_references (live identity, docs/19 §5 'refresh live metadata'); asset_dependencies (visibility_of_usage declaration defaults 'private'); knowledge_publications (publication/visibility record, ADR-006 'Publish controls visibility'; not listed in the append-only sets — exempted rather than over-guarded); subscriptions (user-managed); outbox_events & webhook_deliveries (worker bookkeeping: published_at/attempts/status); search_documents (rebuildable projection, upsert on rebuild). Implementation: one shared guard function + one trigger per table, tgtype=27 (BEFORE, per-row, UPDATE+DELETE), tgenabled='O' on both fresh install and the 13→14 upgrade. Error message names table and operation. goose StatementBegin/StatementEnd wraps the plpgsql body (goose v3 splits statements on semicolons). Existing T0005 tests updated only where the new guard legitimately changed the observable behavior (project_states DELETE now P0001 instead of FK 23503 — the guard fires first; the FK RESTRICT evidence is still present via the users DELETE case). PostgreSQL evidence was gathered on a task-namespaced compose project (posttask-t0013, host port 15433) and all scratch databases were dropped; the container was removed after the run.
